explanation: Greek tragoidia joins tragos, goat, and oide, song. Nobody knows why for certain: one theory points to a goat given as a prize at drama contests for Dionysus.

claims.text: 'Tragedy' comes from Greek tragoidia, from tragos (goat) and oide (song).
The Greek source of 'tragedy' does not mean sad play, masked chorus or fall of kings.
The reason for the goat in the word is uncertain.
One theory links the name to a goat awarded as a prize, or sacrificed, at festivals of Dionysus.
